description:
Why: every number in docs/performance.md is macOS on arm64 ('Linux (every number here is macOS on arm64)'), and the test suite has only been run there: the repo has no CI. Linux has been exercised once, by defk-ds0 (a mix release build in a stock Debian image). defk-dtw.11's resolution puts 'cross-compiling and untested architectures unverified' under the verdict's Limitations; that is honest, but a Linux run would shrink the limitation for the platform most Elixir apps deploy to. Things that could differ: gcc vs clang (the build allows CC), glibc libm vs Apple libm (the one rule needs bit-exact float results; see defk-6g6, sincos fusion), x86-64 vectorisation and the fast-path report's clang remarks (gcc has none), sigsetjmp, and dlopen/library reloading in the hot-upgrade tests.

Scope:
1. Run mix ci (or mix test plus the docs checks) on Linux x86-64 and aarch64 with clang, and on x86-64 with gcc; fix or ticket each failure. Decide where it runs (GitHub Actions on the repo, or a documented local Docker recipe); this choice is the maintainer's.
2. One examples/run_all.exs run on Linux x86-64, recorded in docs/performance.md as its own conditions block (provisional if not a quiet machine), with verdicts that differ from macOS called out.
3. Note in the guides what is supported (compilers, OSes) and what is untested.

Done when: the suite passes on the listed Linux targets (or each failure has a ticket), the run is repeatable from a recipe in the repo, the Linux run_all results are recorded, and the verdict's Limitations line can name what was and wasn't checked.

comments.text: The Valgrind container (defk-96f.3) is ready to become a Linux job here (release-time, not per-CI). Also add CC=clang on glibc to the matrix: defk-o52 crashes on the first raise without its fix.

Re-scoped by the map 'Wayfinder: defk ready for a first Hex release' (2026-10-14). Scope item 1's choice is made: dual CI (GitHub Actions and a local Docker recipe), built by defk-wfi.2, which this ticket now waits on. This ticket keeps: fix or ticket each Linux failure that the matrix shows; add the spread to Defk.Bench.report/1 (the known evidence gap) before the measurement run; one examples/run_all.exs run on Linux x86-64 (native hardware, never emulation), recorded in docs/performance.md as its own conditions block, with verdicts that differ from macOS called out; the supported/untested note in the guides.

Resolution: done, merged to main.
- Suite on Linux: CI run 38608015638 on 4d7f6ba passes on all four labels on native hardware (linux-x86_64-clang, linux-x86_64-gcc, linux-aarch64-clang, macos-arm64-clang). The first Linux runs found four bugs, fixed in defk-wfi.7, .8, .9, .10. Repeatable: ci/README.md (GitHub Actions, act, ci/local.sh).
- Spread: Defk.Bench.report/1 records elixir/defk/native_spread_ms (runs, median, max) and prints them; the best run still sets the verdict.
- Measurement run: .github/workflows/measure.yml (on demand) runs ci/measure.sh = mix defk.examples --bench --all --snapshot --fresh. Run 38608036908 on ubuntu-24.04: AMD EPYC 9V45, 2 vCPUs (a private repo's runner), load 1.5-1.8, provisional. 29/31 examples as claimed; hash_chain 0.98x marginal (macOS 0.55x poor) and batched_levenshtein 3.76x good (macOS 1.73x marginal, on a 73k-word list against 234k). Recorded in docs/performance.md 6.31 with every row against macOS. The workflow run shows failure because those two verdicts differ from their claims; the examples keep their macOS claims.
- Also fixed: geo_nearest crashed in check-only mode (read defk_ms); a bench cache test failed when it ran first.
- Guides: docs/guides/deploying.md 'Where defk is tested' (tested targets; untested: musl, macOS x86-64, Windows, BSDs, 32-bit, cross-compiling).
- Verdict: docs/verdict.md Limitations rewritten: what was checked on Linux since, and what was not (a quiet Linux machine with more cores, musl, macOS x86-64, Windows, cross-compiling).
- Check-only examples on Linux aarch64 (podman): 27/32 before the fixes; the rest were missing tools (cargo, cmake, a word list) and memory in the 8 GB VM; the measure workflow installs the tools.
- Not done: Valgrind as a Linux job (stays manual at release time, ci/README.md).

title: Run the test suite on Linux (x86-64 and aarch64) and record one Linux measurement run
